 Dream11 Co-Founder Harsh Jain Hints At New Platform Introduction By December-End
 BW Online Bureau
 Nov 06, 2026
 # Dream11 
 # Harsh Jain 
 # Dream Sports 
 # Dream11 new platform 
 # fantasy sports 
 # real-money gaming ban 
 The proposed launch comes more than a year after the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, prohibited online real-money games and restricted their promotion and advertising
 Dream11 co-founder and CEO Harsh Jain has hinted at plans to launch a revamped version of the fantasy sports platform by the end of December 2026, as per a media report. 
 In a post on social media platform X, Jain said the brand new Dream11 would be built by sports fans and for sports fans. However, he did not reveal details about its features, business model or exact launch date. 
 The proposed launch comes more than a year after the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, prohibited online real-money games and restricted their promotion and advertising. Following the legislation, Dream11 discontinued its paid contests and shifted towards a watch-along platform, allowing users to follow gameplays by prominent content creators. 
 Dream Sports, Dream11's parent company, has also explored businesses beyond fantasy sports, including wealthtech, stockbroking and SaaS. However, it has scaled back several ventures, shutting down Dream Money, FanCode's sports merchandise business and its AI-powered sports analytics app Dream Play. 
 Its portfolio continues to include FanCode, a sports streaming platform, DreamCricket and the investment platform DreamStreet. 
 The company is also facing GST dues of more than Rs 20,000 Cr. Earlier this year, the Supreme Court upheld the tax authorities' decision to impose 28 per cent retrospective GST on online real-money gaming companies, calculated on the full face value of bets placed through their platforms. 
 The upcoming Dream11 platform could mark a new phase for the company, although its features and business model remain undisclosed.
